brief: The Nasdaq 100 fell 3.4% on month-end Friday, a two-standard-deviation move following Intel's record crash, capping October as the index's worst month of the year. Goldman's Chris Lucas reports US ETFs took in just over $200bn in October, the second-largest month on record, pushing 2026 YTD inflows to $1.7tn, above 2025's full-year $1.45tn record. ETFs that underperformed the Nasdaq, led by semis, drew 2.4% of assets versus 0.8% for outperformers; SOXL alone took in a record $7bn as the SOX had its worst week of the year. Levered ETFs had their largest inflow month ever (+$13bn), including a record $3bn on the Friday selloff, even as Nomura's McElligott warned of a $35bn rebalancing dump into the close. Goldman's Coppersmith says professional risk appetite saw its biggest five-year plunge even as retail leveraged up, and Sharkey notes the Nasdaq trailed the equal-weight S&P by 12%, the worst since 2002. The following Monday, oil fell over 7% on US-Iran talk hopes and the Nasdaq closed in a 10% correction, leaving Friday's levered buying underwater. The piece sides with the pros that further downside will be decided by rebalancing flows, not fundamentals, while noting the bull case of $1.7tn in buying power.
